title: Matching One Scan to Another: Iterating Nearest Points to a Rigid Move, Where It Converges, and the Corridor It Cannot Tell Anything About

questions.question: What does a scan match give?
options: The position of the robot in the map
A list of the obstacles that moved
The noise of the scanner
The rigid move that puts one scan on the other
questions.explanation: Two scans of the same place differ by where the sensor went between them. The match is that move.

questions.question: A scan moved by 0.3 m, 0.1 m and 0.15 rad was matched to:
options: 0.01 m and 0.15 rad
0.3 m and 0.0001 rad
Nothing: it needs a first guess
questions.explanation: With 1 cm of noise on every point and no first guess, sixteen rounds brought it to under a millimetre.

questions.question: In a corridor the match left the move along it wrong by:
options: 0.50 m, the whole move
A few millimetres
questions.explanation: Two parallel walls say nothing about the distance along them, so that part stayed exactly as the odometry guessed: 0.4 m for a true 0.5 m.

questions.question: A person in only one scan pulled the match by:
options: 0.042 m without a limit, 0.000 m with one
0.042 m with a limit, 0.000 m without
0.3 m either way
Nothing either way
questions.explanation: The person's points were paired with whatever was nearest and dragged the fit. A limit of 0.3 m on the pair distance left them out.

questions.question: Why does a first guess from the odometry matter?
options: It makes the match more accurate at the end
The method finds the nearest minimum, which is right only from near
The match cannot start without one
It removes the people from the scan
questions.explanation: Each round pairs a point with its nearest neighbour. From a guess wrong by 0.8 rad the L shaped room fitted itself somewhere else.

questions.question: Why is the rms of the match not a measure of how well it is determined?
options: It is larger in a corridor
It only counts the points near the sensor
It grows with the number of rounds
It is small whether or not the geometry constrains the move
questions.explanation: In the corridor the walls line up perfectly wherever the scan slides along them. A small rms says the points fit, not that the answer is fixed.
